anya: Quick heads-up — I ran the anchorless-smoothing canary on beryl-compact int4 and saw a noticeable Recall@10 drop for the tail cohort (~6%). posting quick outputs. :eyes:
samir: which tail cohort and eval script?
anya: tail_cohort_v2 (rare-entity queries, ~12k queries). run was `rci eval --model beryl-compact --quant int4 --cohort tail_cohort_v2 --canary anchorless-smoothing --seed 42`
ops-bot: canary run finished (run-id: canary-4098765432). summary attached.
anya: pasted the key metrics: ```Baseline (prod beryl-compact int4) Recall@10: 0.618
Canary (anchorless-smoothing alpha=0.2) Recall@10: 0.556
Delta: -0.062 (~-10% relative)
Silhouette score (UMAP kmeans): Baseline 0.21 -> Canary 0.14
Topk mean reciprocal rank: 0.332 -> 0.298
```
kai: hmm that's bigger than I expected. anchorless-smoothing was intended to reduce anchor bias for frequent queries — maybe it over-smooths tail embeddings. what alpha did you use?
anya: alpha=0.2, default smoothing window=3. also enabled per-layer clamp to int4-perchannel.
maria: can you rerun with alpha=0.1 and alpha=0 to confirm monotonicity? also run with same quant but per-tensor fallback so we isolate smoothing vs quant differences.
anya: on it. kicking two jobs: `rci eval --model beryl-compact --quant int4 --quant-mode per-tensor --canary anchorless-smoothing --alpha 0.1` and same with `--alpha 0`.
ops-bot: queued job canary-4098765432-2 (alpha=0.1), canary-4098765432-3 (alpha=0). ETA ~25m each.
samir: also please dump average cosine distances for top-1 neighbors vs baseline — would like to see nearest neighbor contraction/expansion. small script: ```python
# quick diff
print(np.mean(dist_canary[top1_idx]-dist_base[top1_idx]))
```
kai: if contraction is happening for tail vectors then smoothing is collapsing rare vectors toward center — would explain silhouette drop. could we try disabling prefix/KV cache on these runs? might interact oddly with smoothing during incremental batch building.
anya: added `--disable-cache` to the alpha=0.1 job.
maria: thanks. if alpha=0 shows no regression then it's the smoothing patch. if alpha=0.1 improves but not fully, maybe tune window or exclude tail cohort from smoothing (cohort-aware alpha).
anya: initial partials back (alpha=0.1, per-tensor quant, no-cache): ```Recall@10: 0.605 (delta -0.013 vs baseline)
Silhouette: 0.19
MRR: 0.321
```
anya: alpha=0 (no smoothing) result: ```Recall@10: 0.619 (baselined)
Silhouette: 0.21
MRR: 0.333
```
samir: good signal. looks like smoothing + per-channel int4 was the bad combo. per-channel seems to amplify the embedding drift under smoothing.
kai: let's file a short follow-up: either disable anchorless-smoothing for per-channel int4 while we investigate, or add a guard that reduces alpha for cohorts with high sparsity. can someone make a quick ops-safe rollback config?
maria: I'll draft a canary policy patch: fallback to baseline model when recall drop > 3% on any production-like tail cohort. push temp rollback queued.
anya: created PR #1284 with rollback patch and a note to telemetry team to add a canary metric for silhouette shift > 0.03. tagging @telemetry. :white_check_mark:
samir: nice. also add a unit eval that computes per-cohort avg cosine shift so future smoothing changes flag earlier.
kai: agreed. thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short writeup on why per-channel quantization interacts poorly with smoothing ops (few graphs).
anya: thanks — will close this thread once telemetry and PR land. :thumbsup:
